docs.title: About deep-research-client
docs.text: Wrapper for multiple deep research tools

docs.title: Template Support
docs.text: The deep-research-client supports both f-string style templates and Jinja2 templates, allowing you to create flexible, reusable research queries.

docs.title: F-String Templates (Legacy)
docs.text:
F-string templates use simple {variable} placeholders:

Research the {gene} gene in {organism}.

These templates are straightforward and work well for simple variable substitution.

docs.title: Jinja2 Templates
docs.text:
Jinja2 templates offer advanced features including: - Conditional logic - Loops - Filters and transformations - Template inheritance

Example with conditionals:

Research the {{gene}} gene in {{organism}}.
{% if detail_level == "high" %}
Include detailed information about:
- Molecular function
- Biological processes
- Known mutations
{% else %}
Provide a brief overview.
{% endif %}

Example with loops:

Research topics for {{gene}}:
{% for topic in topics %}
- {{topic}}
{% endfor %}

docs.title: Format Detection
docs.text: The template format is automatically detected based on:

docs.title: 1. File Extension
docs.text:
Files with these extensions are treated as Jinja2 templates: - .j2 - .jinja - .jinja2

Examples: - gene_research.md.j2 → Jinja2 - query.jinja → Jinja2 - template.md → F-string (default)

docs.title: 2. YAML Frontmatter
docs.text:
For .md files, you can specify the format in YAML frontmatter:

---
format: jinja
description: Advanced gene research template
---
Research the {{gene}} gene{% if organism %} in {{organism}}{% endif %}.

Supported format values: - jinja, jinja2 → Jinja2 format - fstring, f-string, python → F-string format

docs.title: 3. Default Behavior
docs.text: If no extension or frontmatter indicates the format: - Default: F-string (for backward compatibility)

docs.title: Using Templates with the CLI
docs.text:
# F-string template
deep-research-client research \
  --template templates/gene_family.md \
  --var family=HOX

# Jinja2 template with file extension
deep-research-client research \
  --template templates/gene_jinja.md.j2 \
  --var gene=BRCA1 \
  --var organism=human \
  --var detail_level=high

# Jinja2 template with frontmatter
deep-research-client research \
  --template templates/gene_frontmatter.md \
  --var gene=TP53 \
  --var organism=mouse

docs.title: Using Templates Programmatically
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from deep_research_client.processing import TemplateProcessor

tp = TemplateProcessor()

# Render an f-string template
result = tp.render_template(
    Path('templates/gene_family.md'),
    {'family': 'HOX'}
)

# Render a Jinja2 template
result = tp.render_template(
    Path('templates/gene_jinja.md.j2'),
    {
        'gene': 'BRCA1',
        'organism': 'human',
        'detail_level': 'high'
    }
)

# Process template with metadata
rendered_query, metadata = tp.process_template(
    Path('templates/gene_jinja.md.j2'),
    {'gene': 'BRCA1', 'organism': 'human', 'detail_level': 'high'}
)
# metadata contains: template_file, template_variables, template_format

docs.title: Example 1: Simple F-String Template
docs.text:
File: templates/simple_gene.md

Research the {gene} gene in {organism}.

Usage:

deep-research-client research --template templates/simple_gene.md \
  --var gene=TP53 --var organism=human

docs.title: Example 2: Jinja2 with Conditionals
docs.text:
File: templates/detailed_gene.md.j2

Research the {{gene}} gene in {{organism}}.

{% if include_mutations %}
Focus on:
- Known pathogenic mutations
- Structural variants
- Clinical significance
{% endif %}

{% if include_expression %}
Include expression data:
- Tissue specificity
- Developmental stages
- Disease states
{% endif %}

Usage:

deep-research-client research --template templates/detailed_gene.md.j2 \
  --var gene=BRCA1 \
  --var organism=human \
  --var include_mutations=true \
  --var include_expression=true

docs.title: Example 3: Jinja2 with Loops
docs.text:
File: templates/multi_topic.md.j2

Comprehensive research on {{gene}}:

{% for topic in topics %}
## {{topic|title}}

Provide detailed information about {{gene}} related to {{topic}}.

{% endfor %}

Usage:

from pathlib import Path
from deep_research_client.processing import TemplateProcessor

tp = TemplateProcessor()
result = tp.render_template(
    Path('templates/multi_topic.md.j2'),
    {
        'gene': 'TP53',
        'topics': ['function', 'expression', 'mutations', 'pathways']
    }
)

docs.title: Example 4: Frontmatter-Based Format
docs.text:
File: templates/frontmatter_example.md

---
format: jinja
author: Research Team
version: 1.0
---
# {{title}}

Research question: {{question}}

{% if background %}
## Background
{{background}}
{% endif %}

## Specific Questions
{% for q in specific_questions %}
{{loop.index}}. {{q}}
{% endfor %}

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Jinja2 includes many built-in filters:

Gene: {{gene|upper}}
Organism: {{organism|capitalize}}
Date: {{date|default('2024-01-01')}}

docs.title: Conditionals
docs.text:
{% if condition %}
  content when true
{% elif other_condition %}
  alternative content
{% else %}
  default content
{% endif %}

docs.title: Loops
docs.text:
{% for item in list %}
  - {{item}}
{% endfor %}

{% for key, value in dict.items() %}
  {{key}}: {{value}}
{% endfor %}

docs.title: Inline Conditionals
docs.text: Research {{gene}}{% if organism %} in {{organism}}{% endif %}.

docs.title: Metadata Tracking
docs.text:
When using templates, the output includes metadata about the template used:

---
provider: openai
model: gpt-4
template_file: templates/gene_jinja.md.j2
template_format: jinja
template_variables:
  gene: BRCA1
  organism: human
  detail_level: high
---

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use file extensions for clarity (.j2 for Jinja2 templates)
  2. Add frontmatter to .md files when using Jinja2 features
  3. Keep it simple - use f-strings for basic substitution
  4. Use Jinja2 when you need:
  5. Conditional content
  6. Loops over lists
  7. Filters and transformations
  8. Complex logic
  9. Document your templates with frontmatter metadata
  10. Test templates with various variable combinations

docs.title: Migration Guide
docs.text:
If you have existing f-string templates:

  1. No changes needed - they continue to work as-is
  2. Optional upgrade - convert to .md.j2 or add frontmatter if you want Jinja2 features
  3. Gradual adoption - mix both formats in the same project

Example migration:

Before (f-string):

Research {gene} in {organism}.

After (Jinja2 with enhancements):

Research {{gene}}{% if organism %} in {{organism}}{% endif %}.

{% if detail_level == "comprehensive" %}
Include:
- Molecular function
- Disease associations
- Expression patterns
{% endif %}

docs.title: Template Variables Not Found
docs.text:
Error: Missing template variables: gene, organism

Solution: Ensure all required variables are provided via --var flags or in the variables dictionary.

docs.title: Jinja2 Syntax Errors
docs.text:
Error: TemplateSyntaxError: unexpected '}'

Solution: Check that Jinja2 templates use {{variable}} (double braces), not {variable} (single braces).

docs.title: Format Not Detected
docs.text:
Issue: Template uses Jinja2 syntax but is parsed as f-string.

Solution: - Rename file with .j2 extension, or - Add frontmatter with format: jinja
